newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share market opens with gentle buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share market opens with gentle buying.

text.p: The Singapore share market was slightly firmer early Thursday morning after investors had discounted Singapore's weak economic data, dealers said.
At 0145 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index rose 7.30 points to 2,087.75 on a slim market volume of 19 million shares.

"What we are seeing is a gentle erosion of stock prices. I don't think there will be any sudden movement where investors panic," a dealer with a local broking firm said. "The market has discounted the weak economy," he said.
Dealers noted gentle buying came in to support stocks as their prices eased.
Late Tuesday, Singapore announced third quarter gross domestic product growth fell to 3.2 percent from second quarter's 7.5 percent.
"What matters is how (we are going) to manage a soft landing," one dealer said.
Speculative and small capitalised stocks dominated activity. Recently-listed Labroy Marine headed the actives with 2.5 million shares and was up Singapore $0.05 (US$0.035) to S$1.28.
Sembawang Corp and Keppel Corp rose S$0.20 each to S$6.65 and S$10.40 respectively. Singapore Press foreign slipped S$0.10 to S$24.10.
